overview: A rare archival gospel compilation capturing the vibrant musical life of Oakwood College during the 1985–86 school year. Recorded live across the Oakwood College and Alabama A&M University campuses, this collection showcases an extraordinary lineup of student ensembles, choirs, quartets, and soloists whose performances helped shape the legacy of Adventist gospel music.  Featuring beloved groups such as The Aeolians, A Special Blend, Alliance, Foundation, Unity, His Own, and the Blessed Peace Choir, the video highlights a wide range of spirituals, anthems, contemporary gospel selections, and traditional favorites. The program also includes appearances by celebrated baritone Wintley Phipps and the Oakwood College Choir.  Preserved and released by Black In The Day Adventist Productions, this compilation serves as a historical time capsule—celebrating African‑American Adventist musical heritage and the unforgettable “precious memories” of Oakwood’s campus worship culture.

With first-hand recollections from David's mother and the doctors, nurses, therapists, and the chaplain who cared for him, as well those who were critical of the handling of his case, this film documents the life of a little boy who became a living experiment in a fight to cure a rare disease.

overview: The concert, recorded on December 14, 1986, was the final performance of Elton John's "Tour De Force" tour in Australia and New Zealand. It featured two sets: the first with John's 14-piece band, including backing vocalists and horn section, showcasing his flamboyant stage persona, and the second with the band joined by the 88-piece Melbourne Symphony Orchestra, with John dressed as Mozart. The concert highlighted his band lineup from the "Leather Jackets" album and featured new orchestral arrangements by James Newton Howard. The recording focuses on the second half of the show, with some tracks omitted. It marked the end of John's iconic stage costumes, a tradition he had maintained since the early 1970s, and was his last performance before undergoing successful throat surgery in January 1987, which would alter his voice and temporarily halt his touring.

overview: In the Hudson River region of New York lies Holy Cross Monastery, an Anglican Benedictine monastery whose monks follow an ancient guidebook for monastic living known as The Rule. It was written by St. Benedict of Nursia 1500 years ago during a period when the Western Roman Empire was in a state of collapse. The spirit of the Rule emphasizes pax (peace) and ora et labora (pray and work), fostering a balanced life of community, spiritual growth, and service to God. Its core values are humility, obedience, and simplicity. Producer/director John Decker crafts an ethereal meditation on the rhythms and rituals of the everyday life of 21st century monks living in community together. Portrait of a Monastery creates an ode to a way of life that is vital to this historical moment as an antidote to the division and violence that plague our world.

title: Deep Soup
overview: Digital technology is increasingly steering us towards a world of the mind, a frictionless existence that has become detached from our physical experience. With this film, post-humanist artists Luna Maurer and Roel Wouters attempt to turn the tide. They seek a way to lead people back from their screens to a bodily and material experience.  The duo invited people online to contribute their own videos on a variety of themes. Not of people, but only of matter and movement—breaking, rolling, sinking, floating, falling. All these clips go into the soup—a green physical intelligence that is trained on the collected images.  In Deep Soup, we see this non-human intelligence in its weightless world, processing this slurry of information. The result is a challenge to view physical reality with fresh eyes. A celebration of the forces that belong to our material world, which digital AI models and algorithms try to smooth out.

title: The Nanyang Volunteers
overview: When China’s coast collapsed in 1937, a lifeline was forced through the mountains: the Burma Road. Along it came thousands of overseas Chinese from Southeast Asia - later called the Nanyang Mechanics - returning to a homeland many had never seen to keep the war effort alive. This documentary revives their nearly forgotten story through survivor interviews, descendants’ memories, and archival footage, tracing the perilous journey from Kunming’s training grounds to the bombed‑out front. They faced disease, air raids, impossible roads, and disappearance into occupied territory; some survived only by blending into remote Yi villages. Over a thousand never returned, leaving families with no graves, only silence. The film restores the legacy of the 3,193 volunteers who kept China’s last lifeline open when the world was closing in.

Inspired by Portal 2, the project reimagines the universe of the iconic game through a darker, atmospheric, and cinematic lens. Combining practical filmmaking techniques, visual effects, and environmental storytelling, the short explores the abandoned and mysterious world of Aperture Science while expanding upon the unsettling tone hidden within the original game's setting.
